title: Layerwise Adaptive Mosaic + Prefill Optimizer for Attention Kernel Stability
creator: Priya Raman
description: Investigate and implement a layerwise 'mosaic' for attention kernel selection plus a prefill optimizer that coordinates kernel activation and decode pacing to mitigate tail-latency regressions observed when mixing FlashAttention v2 and v3 and various quantized runtimes. Goal: reduce p95/p99 decode latency regressions for mixed-precision, long-context workloads while preserving throughput and cost targets.
background: Recent rollouts of FlashAttention v3 variants exposed intermittent p95/p99 spikes on long-context customers using per-tenant quantized model variants. Existing selectors pick kernels per-request with coarse heuristics (shape thresholds) which oscillate during bursts. We suspect per-layer shape/precision interactions and cold KV cache handoffs drive oscillation and decode jitter. This ticket proposes a per-layer score-mosaic and a prefill optimizer that smooths kernel handoff across prefill->decode boundary.
goals: Develop a per-layer kernel scoring model (lightweight heuristics + telemetry features) to choose stable kernel ensembles for a request instead of per-stage single-kernel flips
Build Prefill Optimizer that (1) smooths kernel handoff when context transitions from prefill to decode and (2) staggers v3 activations to avoid simultaneous warmups
Canary rollout with safety gates that limit p95 regression to <2% vs baseline and improve p99 by >=5% on targeted workloads
design_decisions: Score inputs: layer_dim, head_count, seq_prefill_len, seq_decode_len, batch_size, precision_hint, cached_kv_bytes
Decision: use an ensemble of three kernel candidates (v2, v3, quantized) per-layer and select a composite plan that minimizes expected tail-latency risk rather than instant throughput

Prefill smoothing: introduce a small handshake window (configurable ms) during which prefill chooses the lower-variance kernel even if it's slightly higher-cost; decode may ramp to higher-throughput kernel after stable telemetry
implementation_plan: 1) Telemetry: add layer-level shape/precision tagging to attention decision traces (ENG-421999)
2) Offline calibration: run synthetic matrix of (layers x seq_len x batch x precision) to build scoring table
3) Runtime: implement MosaicSelector component that returns a per-request per-layer plan; integrate into kernel router
4) Prefill Optimizer: implement prefill->decode handshake and ramp logic; expose config flags for canary
5) Canary: 1% traffic with rollback on SLI breach; extend to 10% if stable
6) Post-canary rollout with gradual ramp and observe cost/quality trade-offs
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: added decision latency in selector path could increase median latency. Mitigation: cache per-model signature decisions and precompute for popular shapes
Risk: higher token cost from conservative prefill choices. Mitigation: expose per-tenant policy to relax conservatism for cost-sensitive customers
Risk: new telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample 10% of requests for detailed layer traces initially
test_plan: Synthetic bench matrix (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/attn-bench) covering seq lengths 64..8192, batch 1..8, precisions fp16/int8/awq
A/B canary with shadow traffic capture for 48 hours; compare p50/p95/p99 and token-cost delta
Regression harness: run existing hybrid regression suite (ENG-53241 harness) and add mosaic-specific scenarios
telemetry_queries: query: SELECT percentile_latency(95), percentile_latency(99) FROM decode_traces WHERE model='llama-2-13b' AND seq_len>1024 AND kernel_activation='v3' GROUP BY kernel, layer_dim
query: count_if(trace->tag=='mosaic_handoff' AND trace.result='fallback') AS fallbacks_per_minute FROM attention_traces WHERE env='canary'
